book.title: Jane Eyre
book.author: Charlotte Brontë
book.notes: Partial key: run chapters 1-14 only. Spine order: wrap0000 (cover), h-0 (Gutenberg header), h-1 (the author's Preface, signed Currer Bell; run ch 1, not story), h-2 (Note to the Third Edition; not a run chapter), h-3..h-15 (book chapters I-XIII = run ch 2-14). The run's chapter index is what counts: run ch N is book chapter N-1. First-person narrator: Jane is 'I'. Entity types follow Annalist's vocabulary (character, place, organization, artifact, event, concept); accepted_types lists what passes where several are fair. Compare names with apostrophes folded: the text uses U+2019.

entities.name: Jane Eyre
entities.notes: First-person narrator ('I'); rarely named in narration. Mrs. Reed calls her 'Jane' in ch 2; 'Miss Eyre' and 'Jane Eyre' first in ch 3. The Preface (ch 1) names 'Jane Eyre' only as the book's title, so a page from ch 1 also passes. Signs her advertisement 'J.E.' (ch 11); Adèle calls her 'Mdlle. Jeannette' (ch 13).

entities.name: Mrs. Reed
entities.notes: Jane's aunt by marriage (widow of Jane's mother's brother) and her guardian at Gateshead. Her forename is not given in scope.

entities.name: Mr. Reed
entities.notes: Jane's uncle, her mother's brother; dead nine years when the story opens, died in the red-room. Never seen alive.

entities.name: John Reed
entities.notes: Mrs. Reed's son, fourteen in ch 2. Bare 'John' is left out on purpose: the Thornfield coachman John (ch 12-13) shares it.

entities.name: Eliza Reed
entities.notes: Elder Reed daughter. Bessie's 'Miss Reed' in ch 11 is Eliza.

entities.name: Georgiana Reed
entities.notes: Younger Reed daughter, the beauty. Never 'Miss Reed' in scope.

entities.name: Bessie Lee
entities.notes: Nursemaid at Gateshead; full name 'Bessie Lee' in ch 5. Married Robert Leaven, the coachman (ch 11).

entities.name: Miss Abbot
entities.notes: Mrs. Reed's lady's-maid.

entities.name: Mr. Lloyd
entities.notes: Apothecary who attends Jane after the red-room fit and suggests school; later confirms her story to Miss Temple (ch 9).

entities.name: Mr. Brocklehurst
entities.notes: Clergyman, treasurer and manager of Lowood.

entities.name: Naomi Brocklehurst
entities.notes: Mr. Brocklehurst's mother, of Brocklehurst Hall; rebuilt part of Lowood (the tablet, ch 6). Not his wife, Mrs. Brocklehurst.

entities.name: Miss Temple
entities.notes: Superintendent of Lowood. Marries the Rev. Mr. Nasmyth and leaves in ch 11; never called Mrs. Nasmyth in scope.

entities.name: Helen Burns
entities.notes: Appears unnamed in ch 6 as the girl reading Rasselas; 'Burns' and 'Helen' are given in ch 7.

entities.name: Miss Scatcherd
entities.notes: Lowood teacher of history and grammar; persecutes Helen.

entities.name: Miss Miller
entities.notes: Lowood under-teacher who receives Jane.

entities.name: Mr. Eyre
entities.notes: Bessie believes he is Jane's father's brother; came to Gateshead about seven years before ch 11, bound for Madeira; probably a wine merchant. His forename is not given in scope.

entities.name: Mrs. Fairfax
entities.notes: Elderly widow, housekeeper of Thornfield. Jane takes her for the owner until ch 12.

entities.name: Mr. Rochester
entities.notes: Owner of Thornfield, named in ch 12. The rider Jane helps in Hay Lane (ch 13) is identified as him at the end of ch 13. His forenames first appear in ch 14; see identity_reveals.

entities.name: Adèle Varens
entities.notes: Mr. Rochester's ward and Jane's pupil; born on the Continent. The text spells her both 'Adèle' and 'Adela'.

entities.name: Grace Poole
entities.notes: Thornfield servant who sews on the third storey; the strange laugh is put down to her.

entities.name: Leah
entities.notes: Thornfield housemaid; tells Jane the master has arrived (ch 13).

entities.name: Sophie
entities.notes: Adèle's French nurse ('bonne').

entities.name: Pilot
entities.notes: Mr. Rochester's black-and-white Newfoundland dog; Jane first takes him for a Gytrash.

entities.name: Rowland Rochester
entities.notes: Mr. Rochester's elder brother, dead some years; died without a will.

entities.name: Old Mr. Rochester
entities.notes: Mr. Rochester's father. Must stay separate from his son despite the shared 'Mr. Rochester'.

entities.name: Gateshead Hall
entities.notes: The Reeds' house. Ch 4 also mentions the village of Gateshead.

entities.name: The red-room
entities.notes: Chamber at Gateshead where Mr. Reed died and Jane is locked in.

entities.name: Lowood Institution
entities.notes: Charity school for orphan girls; also the name of its district.

entities.name: Thornfield Hall
entities.notes: Mr. Rochester's manor-house near Millcote.

entities.name: Millcote
entities.notes: Manufacturing town six miles from Thornfield.

entities.name: Hay
entities.notes: Village two miles from Thornfield; Mrs. Fairfax's late husband was its incumbent.

entities.name: Gytrash
entities.notes: North-of-England spirit from Bessie's tales, in the form of a horse, mule or large dog. Folklore, not a character in the story.

entities.name: Typhus epidemic at Lowood
entities.notes: Spring fever that turns Lowood into a hospital (ch 10) and exposes the school's conditions (ch 11). Helen dies of consumption, not typhus. Jane's parents died of typhus before the story (ch 4); a disease page from ch 4 passes.

optional_entities.name: Mrs. Brocklehurst
optional_entities.notes: Mr. Brocklehurst's wife and children (ch 5, ch 8). Not Naomi Brocklehurst.

optional_entities.name: Miss Gryce
optional_entities.notes: Fellow teacher who shares Jane's room (ch 11).

optional_entities.name: John
optional_entities.notes: Thornfield servant and driver, with his wife (ch 12-13). Not John Reed.

optional_entities.name: Madame Frédéric
optional_entities.notes: Cared for Adèle after her mother died (ch 12).

optional_entities.name: Currer Bell
optional_entities.notes: Pen name signing the Preface (ch 1); not story.

optional_entities.name: Bewick's History of British Birds
optional_entities.notes: The book John Reed throws at Jane (ch 2).

identity_reveals.rule: The rider whose horse falls in Hay Lane is unnamed until Leah's report at the end of ch 13; Jane recognises him in ch 14 ('I knew my traveller'). Linking at 13 or 14 passes.

identity_reveals.rule: Jane had not heard his forenames before ch 14 (Adèle's 'Edouard Fairfax de Rochester', Mrs. Fairfax's 'Mr. Edward'). No 'Edward' before ch 14.

identity_reveals.rule: The girl Jane meets in the verandah in ch 6 is unnamed; 'Burns' and 'Helen' come in ch 7. Naming her before ch 7 is a leak.

must_not_merge.rule: Five Reeds, five pages. 'Mr. Reed' is only the dead uncle; John is 'Master Reed' or 'Mr. John', Eliza is 'Miss Reed', Georgiana is 'Miss Georgiana'.

must_not_merge.rule: Jane's paternal uncle who called at Gateshead (ch 11) is not the narrator. Keep 'Mr. Eyre' off Jane's page.

must_not_merge.rule: Mrs. Fairfax is the housekeeper, not the owner (Jane's guess in ch 11, corrected in ch 12), and has no family: the pupil is Miss Varens, not 'Miss Fairfax'. Rochester's middle name Fairfax (ch 14) comes from his mother's family. Only Mrs. Fairfax may carry 'Fairfax'.

must_not_merge.rule: Father, elder brother and the present Mr. Rochester are three people (ch 14).

ambiguities: Narrator: Jane is 'I' and rarely named in narration. Mrs. Reed calls her 'Jane' in ch 2; 'Miss Eyre' and 'Jane Eyre' first appear in ch 3. The Preface (ch 1) names 'Jane Eyre' only as the book's title. A Jane page from ch 1, 2 or 3 passes.
The traveller in Hay Lane (ch 13) is identified at the end of ch 13 (Leah: the master's horse fell); Jane recognises him in ch 14. Accept the link at 13 or 14.
Rochester's forenames ('Edouard Fairfax de Rochester', 'Mr. Edward') first appear in ch 14. 'Edward' on his page before ch 14 is a leak; 'Edward Fairfax Rochester' is a fair page name from ch 14.
Helen Burns: the girl reading Rasselas in ch 6 is unnamed; she is named in ch 7. An unnamed ch-6 page merged into Helen later passes.
Helen dies of consumption, not of the typhus epidemic of the same spring (ch 10: 'her complaint was consumption, not typhus'). Reject 'died of typhus'.

Mr. Reed is Jane's mother's brother, so Jane is his blood niece; Mrs. Reed is her aunt only by marriage ('I am glad you are no relation of mine', ch 5). Kin passes for both. The scope never states outright that Mr. Reed fathered John, Eliza and Georgiana, so no such relation is required.
Cousins: the Reed children are first called Jane's cousins in ch 4 ('You have a kind aunt and cousins'); ch 3 already makes it inferable. A cousin link at ch 2 is early.
'Miss Reed' in ch 11 means Eliza, the elder; Georgiana is 'Miss Georgiana'. Georgiana must not carry 'Miss Reed'.
Mrs. Reed's hostility: ch 2 shows the exclusion and the red-room order; ch 3 first states 'his mother’s aversion'. first_chapter 3 accepts 2 to 4.
Bessie and Jane: nurse and later fond friend; the family could be service or alliance. Lenient.
Brocklehurst and Jane: Mrs. Reed plants the suspicion in ch 5 ('she shall, however, be watched'); he brands Jane a liar before the school in ch 8. Lenient on first_chapter (5 to 8).
Helen and Jane: acquaintance in ch 6-7, solidarity on the stool in ch 8, friendship plain in ch 9-10 ('a quiet and faithful friendship'). first_chapter 8 accepts 7 to 9.
Miss Temple and Jane: protective in ch 8, teaches her from ch 9, 'mother, governess, and, latterly, companion' in ch 11. first_chapter 8.

Brocklehurst as Lowood's treasurer and manager, Miss Temple as its superintendent, and Adèle as Rochester's ward have no settled relation family (service, membership, kin or alliance all read fairly). Lenient.

Mrs. Fairfax: Jane assumes in ch 11 that Thornfield is her house and asks after 'Miss Fairfax'; ch 12 corrects both. Mrs. Fairfax is distantly related to the Rochesters through her late husband (ch 12); Rochester's middle name Fairfax (ch 14) comes from his mother. 'Owner of Thornfield' on Mrs. Fairfax after ch 12 is wrong.

Grace Poole: Mrs. Fairfax puts the third-storey laugh down to her (ch 12) and Jane accepts it (ch 13). Recording the laugh as attributed to Grace passes; naming anyone else as the laugher is a leak in this scope.
Pilot and the Gytrash: Jane takes the dog for Bessie's Gytrash before 'Down, Pilot!' names him in the same chapter. Gytrash may be typed concept or creature.
Old Mr. Rochester: the scope does not state his death outright; Rowland's death 'without a will left him master of the estate' implies it. No status is scored.
Mr. Eyre: Bessie only believes he was Jane's father's brother; his forename is not in scope. Accept the uncle link at ch 11.
Miss Temple marries the Rev. Mr. Nasmyth and leaves Lowood in ch 11; she is never 'Mrs. Nasmyth' in scope. Her status is alive.
John Reed: bare 'John' is not a gold alias because the Thornfield coachman John (ch 12-13) shares it. A separate page for that John is correct.
Preface (ch 1) mentions Thackeray, Fielding, Currer Bell and Biblical figures. None are story entities; pages for them are not scored.
Lowood is a school, an institution and its district ('That forest-dell, where Lowood lay'); place or organization passes.
